title: Enabling Data-Deduplication-Assisted Data Relocation for Interlaced Magnetic Recording
problem: Interlaced Magnetic Recording (IMR) hard drives suffer degraded performance when updating data on overlapped tracks, requiring rewriting up to two tracks per update.
motivation: IMR drives overlap tracks to increase storage capacity in post-AI era; but update-induced track rewrites create performance bottleneck. Existing hot/cold separation ignores data deduplication opportunities.
method: Leverages data deduplication metadata (reference counts) to guide data relocation in IMR drives. Deduplicated data (static unless references drop to one) can be placed/migrated to overlapped tracks without inducing future rewrites. Replaces frequency-based hot/cold tracking with deduplication-informed placement.
key_novelty: First application of deduplication reference counts to data relocation in IMR drives, enabling zero-cost overlap placement.
contributions: Deduplication-assisted data relocation strategy for IMR drives
Reference count-based placement vs frequency-based hot/cold separation
37.57% average reduction in accumulated read/write latency vs SOTA IMR schemes
limitations: Evaluation assumes data deduplication enabled; effectiveness without active deduplication not explored.
primary_theme: Deduplication-aware data placement in IMR drives
